events.title: Cycle 2999.08 statement issued
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the present statement cycle is 2999.08. Active meters: 214,116,882. Reads continue every four seconds. Estimated reads issued since 2041: zero.

events.title: This meter notes the cycle
events.body: This meter has recorded every read since 2091. Cycle 2999.08 is no exception. The sum is acceptable. The interval is acceptable. This meter remains.

events.title: Yard glass read lag
events.body: The Sheb's south bay yard glass reported a four-second read at 08:59:56 and then nothing until 09:00:04. Eight seconds. We counted. If billing follows the house, the house would like its missing four seconds accounted for.

events.title: Acknowledgment: New Sheboygan read timing
events.body: In-Space Power acknowledges the report from New Sheboygan, Tow Route 4. The interval at 08:59:56 was a scheduled synchronization pulse, not a missed read. No charge was issued for the interval. The house is not billed for sync.

events.title: On the matter of shade pricing
events.body: We, Europa Autonomous Grid, note that shade rates are cited as pricier because stored light has already been carried. We find this framing acceptable. We have paid our own bill since 2093. We will continue.

events.title: Footnote: Europa payment status
events.body: Correction to record: a community post elsewhere claimed Europa 'used to be behind.' Per ledger, Europa Autonomous Grid has paid its own bill without interruption since cycle 2093.001. The claim is rejected.

events.title: Beam shadow on Route 4
events.body: Dredge-Clear reports The Beam cuts out for eighteen minutes when New Sheboygan passes through the relay geometry. Not a fault, just geometry. But my hull is on Underway rate, flat. I pay while the town's yard glass sits in my shadow. Explain that.

events.title: We remember shadows
events.body: Halverson Green remembers when a shadow meant a cloud over the cornfield. Now shadows come from our own town, and from New Sheboygan ahead of us, and from the tugs. The meter reads every four seconds regardless. That is the agreement.

events.title: Generation mix remains stable
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the generation mix for cycle 2999.08: The Beam 46%, Fusion 31%, Moontide 14%, Stored light 9%. No source reached a retest threshold. The mix is accepted.

events.title: This meter accepts the mix
events.body: This meter has seen mixes change. Once, in 2112, stored light reached 34%. This meter remembers. The present mix is acceptable. This meter remains.

events.title: Cycle 2999.09 Opening
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the opening of statement cycle 2999.09. The active meter inventory stands at 214,116,882 units, each reporting at four-second intervals. The generation mix for this cycle remains The Beam at 46 percent, Fusion at 31 percent, Moontide at 14 percent, and Stored light at 9 percent. Billing follows the house.

events.title: Statement 2999.09 Noted
events.body: Europa notes the opening of cycle 2999.09 and the unchanged four-second cadence across 214,116,882 meters. We recorded the same generation percentages at the close of 2999.08 and will continue reconciling our accounts on our own schedule. The house is billed. Europa pays its own.

events.title: Shadow Over Millerton Station
events.body: This meter records that Millerton Station on Tow-Route 4 has sat in the shadow of New Lancaster orbital for forty-three cycles. The shade rate of 0.0114 credits per megajoule applies to reads that register no direct beam. This meter does not question the rate. This meter questions the sum when a town pays for light that arrives as another town's shadow. This meter remembers when Ohio had weather that moved.

events.title: Millerton Station Shade Classification Upheld
events.body: In-Space Power confirms that Millerton Station on Tow-Route 4 is classified under the Porchlight tariff: 0.0042 credits per megajoule for sunward reads, 0.0114 credits per megajoule for shade reads. The shade rate applies to any read that registers no direct beam, regardless of whether the occlusion originates from a neighboring structure, an orbital body, or another station's projected penumbra. Billing follows the house; the meter's position determines the rate, not the provenance of the shadow. The First Light exemption applies only to the first three cycles of a new meter; this read occurs at cycle forty-three. The Corner Main tariff (0.0061/0.0138 credits per megajoule) and the Underway flat rate (0.0088 credits per megajoule) do not apply to this classification.

events.title: Water Tower Classification on Route 4
events.body: Port Cressida's water tower throws beam-shadow across my tow. Meter reads it as structure, invoice prices it as porch. Billing follows the house, but a water tower has no house. Ceres can rule on whether a tank counts as a hull before I pay shade rates on plumbing.

events.title: Water Tower Classification, Tow Route 4
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the water tower at Port Cressida is registered in the ledger as a fixed structure and is billed at the Porchlight shade rate of 0.0114 credits/MJ for reads occurring within beam-shadow. Billing follows the house; the principle applies to any metered structure, independent of whether that structure encloses habitable volume or contains plumbing. The classification is correct and the invoice stands.

events.title: Belt Household Balance, Outstanding Since 2087
events.body: I keep my paper statements in a tin box the way my mother kept hers, and the ledger for the Belt households has shown the same outstanding balance since 2087, which is three hundred and twelve years now without a single settlement read coming through. The automatic systems will tell you the account is reconciled if you let them, but I have checked the printouts myself and the numbers do not lie, they only wait. It was easier to keep track when the cornfield on Tow Route 4 was still a cornfield and you could see the arrears growing as plain as stalks.

events.title: Porch Light Through Sync Pulse
events.body: This meter recorded a porch light burning through synchronization pulse 2999.08.31. The shade rate applied at 0.0114 credits per megajoule. This meter does not question the rate. This meter questions the sum. Ohio had weather once and porch lights meant something then.

events.title: Porch Light, Sync Pulse 2999.08.31
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the load at Earth-Reserve-Ohio was billed at the Porchlight shade rate of 0.0114 credits per megajoule during synchronization pulse 2999.08.31. Billing follows the house: any energy drawn while the meter is live is recorded and charged; only the first three cycles of a newly commissioned First Light account are exempt. The sum reflects the integrated draw across the full pulse window, regardless of weather or precedent. The rate is correct and the sum is correct.

events.title: First Light, Third Cycle
events.body: This meter notes settlement ISP-000214116882 enters its third and final cycle under First Light. Reads will remain unbilled through statement 2999.09. On 2999.10 the Porchlight tariff applies, sunward and shade. This meter has recorded every four-second interval since 2091 and does not question the rate. The sum will be what the sum is.

events.title: Stored Light and the Sunward Rate
events.body: By the time this notice reaches Ceres the Sheb will have rotated twice, but I'll ask it anyway: when a joule was captured in sunlight and sat in a battery for three months, does it still count as sunward when it finally hits a porch lamp out here on Tow Route 4. The tariff sheet says sunward gets 0.0042 and shade gets 0.0114, but it don't say what to call light that remembers the sun but ain't seen it since before we passed Jupiter. Our water tower made the tow and so did our meters, and I'd like our folks billed like the light still knows what side of the hull it came from.

events.title: Stored Light Classification on Tow Route 4
events.body: In-Space Power confirms that stored light is billed according to the physical placement of the receiving meter, not the origin of the joule. Under the Porchlight tariff, sunward-facing meters are rated at 0.0042 credits/MJ and shade-facing meters at 0.0114 credits/MJ; these rates apply to all delivered energy regardless of whether it arrived by direct collection or from battery. Billing follows the house. Light that has not seen the sun since Jupiter passage is billed at the shade rate if the meter is mounted on the shade side of the hull, and at the sunward rate if it is not.

events.title: On the Belt Balance, Unadjusted Since 2087
events.body: I keep my paper statements in a tin box the way my mother did when the cornfield was still a cornfield and not this humming hydroponic bay, and if you look back far enough in those pages you will find the Belt households have carried the same balance since 2087, untouched by any automatic read or quarterly adjustment. The Joint Settlement Authority at Ceres has its ledgers and I have mine, and both of them say the same thing that has been said for over nine hundred years: billing follows the house, and some houses have simply stopped answering. I do not trust the machines to tell me otherwise, but the paper does not lie, and the paper says the Belt has been running a tab since before my grandfather took his first read under the porchlight tariff.

events.title: Cycle Review Window Open
events.body: JSA Ceres cracked open the filing window for cycle review. Any hull running a meter best have their reads squared away—auditors don't give a damn about beam-shadow off whatever oversized rig you're dragging. Billing follows the house, and the house keeps receipts. Keep your transponders singing and your ledgers straight.

events.title: Missed Interchange at Marker Twelve and the Dark Stretch Beyond
events.body: I have kept my paper statements since the meter went in on the third of November two seven oh nine and not once have they shown a read for the seconds we drift past the interchange at Marker Twelve, which is to say the automatic system does not see us when the tow route bends away from the old cornfield that is now a hydroponic bay, and I should like to know who is paying for the dark stretch between buoys forty-four and forty-seven because the shade rate was never meant to cover a house that moves through shadow it did not choose. I have written this down on my kitchen table with a proper pen and I will be keeping the receipt.

events.title: Acknowledgment of Missed Reads at Marker Twelve
events.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of the report concerning tow route 4 at Marker Twelve and the interval between buoys forty-four and forty-seven. The missed reads correspond to a scheduled beamline handoff during which the synchronization pulse was withheld for twelve seconds while relay geometry was recalibrated to the hydroponic bay alignment. No charge was issued for the interval; the Underway flat tariff applies only to metered reads, and zero reads were recorded during the handoff window. The shade rate does not apply to underway transit.

events.title: Meter Reading Through the Gap
events.body: I keep my statements on paper because paper does not pretend to have seen what it has not seen, and yet my meter ISP-TR4-HG-044 has been ticking away every four seconds through the relay geometry window when The Beam cuts out, same as when it is shining, and I would like to know who is paying for light that did not arrive. I remember when this bay was a cornfield and the sun came regular, but I do not recall ever being asked to pay for an empty sky. The automatic read does not notice the difference between a beam and no beam, which is why I keep my paper.

events.title: Acknowledgment: ISP-TR4-HG-044, Relay Geometry Window
events.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of report for account ISP-TR4-HG-044 concerning reads recorded during the scheduled relay geometry window at the referenced bay. The meter maintained its four-second cadence through the beamline handoff sequence, as synchronization pulses do not suspend read collection. No charge was issued for the interval; billing follows the house, and the house received no energy. The paper record and the digital record agree on this point.

events.title: Interchange 12 and the Dark Stretch Between
events.body: I have kept my paper statements since the cornfield was still a cornfield, and not one shows a charge for the dark stretch past Interchange 12, missed on the last tow and belonging to nobody's meter now. The automatic reads do not account for it, which is perhaps why nobody has, but I can tell you from my porch that those houses have paid the shade rate for a sunward berth these three cycles. I would like to know who is collecting for that darkness and whether billing follows the house when the house is in between.

events.title: On Europa's Share of the Mix
events.body: I have been looking over my paper statements from the last cycle, the way I always do, and I cannot find anywhere in the printed figures a proper accounting of how much of The Beam's forty-six percent went out toward Europa and who among the rest of us carried that distance on our meters. The automatic reads never show you the weight of the line losses, and they certainly do not volunteer which households absorbed the extra draw when the Jovian run was heavy. I remember when the cornfield where the hydroponic bay sits now used to tell you exactly where every joule went just by looking at the growth, but now we are expected to trust a number that arrives without a signature.

events.title: Interchange 12 Read Gap Acknowledged
events.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of the report concerning Interchange 12 and the unmetered interval along tow-route-4. During the last scheduled relay geometry, a synchronization pulse at the beamline handoff produced a 4.2-second gap in automatic reads; no estimated reads were issued for this interval. Billing follows the house, and where no read exists, no charge is issued. The shade-rate discrepancy for the preceding three cycles is under review and will be reconciled against the porchlight tariff schedule.

events.title: Correction to Record: Europa Settlement Status
events.body: Correction to record: the submitted notice claims 'we are expected to trust a number that arrives without a signature' and implies Europa has not accounted for its share of The Beam's forty-six percent. The ledger shows Europa Autonomous Grid has paid its own bill without interruption since 2093, with no outstanding balance recorded at any read interval. Line losses are apportioned per the principle that 'billing follows the house' and do not transfer to secondary accounts. Paper statements are advisory only; settlement is conducted by the Joint Settlement Authority Ceres under payment route ISP-2041.

events.title: Shade Rate Complaint, Tow Route 4
events.body: New Sheboygan is filing a complaint about being charged shade rates when the only thing casting a shadow on us is the town parked ahead on Tow Route 4. We didn't tow the Sheb out here to sit in someone else's dark, and our water tower made the trip just fine, thank you. I'd ask central billing to sort out whose shadow belongs to who before sending another statement at the shade tariff. The lag on these notices means we've been eating the overcharge since last cycle.

events.title: First Light, explained for the new settlement
events.body: New hull parked at the outer bend asked what First Light actually covers. Three cycles of reads, not billed. After that the meter runs honest like every other hull on the route. Don't go thinking it covers your beam-shadow from towed structures either—just the reads.

events.title: Shade Rate Determination, Tow Route 4
events.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of New Sheboygan's shade rate complaint regarding Tow Route 4. Under the Porchlight tariff, shade rates of 0.0114 credits/MJ apply to all consumption recorded while a structure is occluded from direct solar incidence, regardless of the occluding body's origin or ownership. Billing follows the house; the meter at New Sheboygan's coordinates registered shade conditions, and the applicable rate was assessed accordingly. Re-tariffing would require either relocation to an unoccluded berth or formal reclassification under the Underway flat rate of 0.0088 credits/MJ, neither of which is currently on file.

events.title: Shade Rate Under Permanent Shadow, Tow Route 4
events.body: I have kept my paper statements since the meters went in on the third of November in 2709, and I have watched the shade rate apply month after month while our town has been hitched behind the first tow with nothing but their undercarriage between us and any honest sunlight. The automatic reads do not trouble themselves with the difference between a town that chose the shade and a town that was parked there by the routing office, and they certainly do not remember the cornfield that stood where the hydroponic bay sits now, which at least knew the courtesy of casting its own shadow. I am not disputing that we sit in the shadow of the first town on Tow Route 4, only that the shade tariff presumes a choice none of us were asked to make.

events.title: What First Light Covers (and What It Don't)
events.body: Got a notice from a new settlement out past the belt asking what First Light actually covers, and I'll tell you what I tell everybody: it covers three cycles where the meter reads but you ain't billed, that's it. Ain't a holiday, ain't a waiver, just gives you time to get your breaker box sorted before the credits start counting. The Sheb's water tower went three cycles on First Light back in '11 and we still paid for the coffee machine, so don't go thinking it means free power. Billing follows the house, always has, and after cycle three the porchlight rate kicks in like it does for the rest of us.

events.title: Shade Tariff Application, Tow Route 4
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the shade tariff applies to all metered premises receiving less than direct solar illumination, regardless of routing assignment or prior land use. Porchlight shade is rated at 0.0114 credits per megajoule; Corner Main shade at 0.0138 credits per megajoule; Underway service is billed at a flat 0.0088 credits per megajoule. Billing follows the house. The automatic reads measure incident radiation at the meter face and do not distinguish between elected shade and assigned shadow. Tow Route 4 premises remain classified under the applicable shade tariff for the duration of their current mooring configuration.

events.title: Four-Second Gap on the Yard Glass
events.body: I have kept paper statements since two thousand seventy-nine and in all that time I have never seen the yard glass go blank for a full four seconds, though your people tell me it was only a synchronization pulse doing its work. I do not trust these automatic reads to begin with, and when the glass goes dark like that it puts me in mind of the old cornfield before they paved it over for the hydroponic bay, when at least a person could see what was growing. The pulse may have synchronized something on your end, but my ledger shows a gap where no read came through, and I should very much like to know what becomes of the numbers that fall into that space.

events.title: Dark Stretch at Marker Seven, Tow Route 4
events.body: I have kept my paper statements since the interchange at Marker Seven went dark last cycle, and not one automatic read has accounted for the stretch between buoys 44 and 46 where the tow line drops into shadow for six hours each rotation, though I remember well enough when that same ground grew corn instead of housing a hydroponic bay. If the billing follows the house, as the Authority maintains, then I should like to know which house sits in the dark and pays the Underway flat rate for current that never arrives, and whether the missed interchange at Marker Seven is to be charged to those of us who still read our own meters by lamplight or to the settlement that promised the replacement coupling three cycles ago.

events.title: Acknowledgment: Marker Seven, Tow Route 4
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the reported dark interval at Marker Seven, Tow Route 4, between buoys 44 and 46. The six-hour shadow each rotation corresponds to the scheduled beamline handoff window during which the primary relay geometry rotates through eclipse and the synchronization pulse is withheld until secondary coupling verification is complete. No charge was issued for the interval; reads logged during the handoff window are classified as synchronization gaps and are not billed under the Underway flat tariff. The replacement coupling remains on the settlement work order and is not a billing event.

events.title: Four-Second Gap on Tow Route 4
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the four-second blank interval on the yard glass at Tow Route 4, account on file since 2079. The gap corresponds to a scheduled synchronization pulse during beamline handoff, when relay geometry shifts between primary and secondary collectors. No read was issued for that interval, and no charge has been applied. The interval contains no numbers to account for.

events.title: Meter Running Dark on Relay Shift
events.body: The Beam cut out during Tuesday's relay geometry shift, but ISP-TR4-NS-001 kept right on counting megajoules like nothing happened. We get that the official notices lag a few cycles out here on Tow Route 4, but the Sheb ain't keen on paying for photons that never showed. The water tower survived the whole tow, seems like the meter could learn when to stop running. Billing follows the house, I know, but the house was dark.

events.title: Cycle Review Filed with Ceres
events.body: The Joint Settlement Authority has opened its filing window for the 2999.09 cycle review, which means another round of paperwork before anyone in the Sheb sees a statement. I've submitted ours on time, same as always, though I expect the lag between here and Ceres will stretch out another week or two before they acknowledge receipt. The water tower's read is clean, the town's meter is accounted for, and I'd appreciate it if whoever reviews our file remembers that billing follows the house and not whoever's holding the clipboard that day.

events.title: Tow Route 4 Meter Acknowledgment
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the report from Tow Route 4, account ISP-TR4-NS-001. The relay geometry shift executed a scheduled beamline handoff; the synchronization pulse registered at the meter as a nominal interval read. No charge was issued for the interval. The read was flagged as a handoff artifact and excluded from settlement. Billing follows the house.

events.title: Porch Light on TR4-NS-001 Through Sync Pulse
events.body: Somebody on the Sheb left their porch light burning right through the synchronization pulse last cycle, and I'm the one who gets the lagged notice about it three days later. We all know the water tower made the tow, but that does not mean we leave the fixtures on while the grid is trying to count. Billing follows the house, sure, but common sense ought to follow the pulse. If you are on Porchlight rate, the sunward side is cheap enough without running through a sync window.

events.title: Who Hauled the Moontide
events.body: Europa pulled fourteen percent of the mix this cycle, Moontide rating, and I want to know which hulls ran the tow. We on Route 4 eat beam-shadow from your floating arrays while you park in the Jovian dark and call it generation. Someone carried that iron out there, and it wasn't the company. The meters don't lie, but the manifests might.

events.title: Correction to Record: Europa Settlement Standing
events.body: Correction to record regarding the assertion that "you park in the Jovian dark and call it generation." The ledger shows Europa Autonomous Grid has paid its own bill <small>without interruption</small> since 2093.¹ The Moontide contribution of fourteen percent is accounted for by tidal capture at the Jovian Lagrange stations, not by towed hulls.² Rate disputes do not alter settlement standing.³

events.title: Porch Light on TR4-NS-001 Through Sync Pulse
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the porch light on TR4-NS-001 registered 14.2 megajoules during the synchronization pulse window of cycle 2999.08. Billing follows the house; the ledger records this consumption against the Porchlight rate at 0.0042 credits per megajoule for the sunward-facing fixture. The synchronization pulse does not interrupt metering. Reads continue at four-second intervals regardless of settlement timing, and the account holder of record is billed accordingly.

events.title: Meter Still Spinning When the Beam Ain't
events.body: During the last relay geometry window, The Beam cut out for about forty minutes while our meter ISP-TR4-NS-001 kept right on reading like nothing happened. Folks here in the Sheb are used to a lot of things, but getting billed for sunshine that never arrived is a new one. The notice about it took three cycles to show up on my terminal, which is about par for the course, but I'd appreciate if the reads paused when the power does. Proud the water tower made it out here, but it doesn't run on nothing.

events.title: Four-Second Gap on Yard Glass, New Sheboygan
events.body: Somewhere between one four-second read and the next, the yard glass on ISP-TR4-NS-001 went quiet for a full cycle. Central says it was a synchronization pulse. Out here on Tow Route 4, we call it a gap, and the folks at the Sheb don't much care what Ceres names it as long as the numbers come through. Water tower's still reading fine, for what that's worth.

events.title: Sheb Node Beamline Handoff — Meter ISP-TR4-NS-001
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the report from the Sheb regarding meter ISP-TR4-NS-001. During the scheduled relay geometry window, a beamline handoff to the tertiary relay produced a forty-two-minute interruption in The Beam's delivery to the node. The meter continued its four-second read cadence throughout, as synchronization pulses maintain the local clock independent of beamline status. No charge was issued for the interval; reads logged during the handoff were flagged and excluded from billing.

events.title: Four-Second Read Interval, Tow Route 4, New Sheboygan
events.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of the report concerning meter ISP-TR4-NS-001 on Tow Route 4, New Sheboygan. The missing read corresponds to a scheduled beamline handoff between relay geometries seven and eight, during which the synchronization pulse suppresses local readout for exactly one four-second cycle. No charge was issued for this interval. The yard glass has resumed normal operation and is transmitting at the standard cadence.

events.title: Meter Don't Know Dark from Light
events.body: Beam cuts out while we're threading relay geometry and the hull goes dark, but ISP-UND-7781 keeps its four-second tick like nothing happened. Billing follows the house, they say, and the house don't care if the light's on or not. Been running Route 4 since '87 and still ain't seen a meter that knows the difference between beam-shadow and a proper blackout.

events.title: Sunward Rate Applied to Stored Light, Tow Route 4
events.body: I have kept my paper statements since before they drained the cornfield and made it into a hydroponic bay, and I do not trust these automatic reads to tell me what kind of power I am actually receiving. The statement for this cycle shows I am being charged the sunward rate on power that comes from stored light, which by my understanding has not seen the sun since it was put away in whatever battery they keep it in, and I would like someone at the Joint Settlement Authority on Ceres to clarify whether light kept in the dark still qualifies as sunlight for tariff purposes.

events.title: ISP-UND-7781, Route 4 Beamline Handoff
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the scheduled beamline handoff at relay geometry 4-Theta on 2999.09.14. The four-second synchronization pulse on ISP-UND-7781 continued as specified; the meter records received energy, not delivery intent. No charge was issued for the dark interval—reads during a scheduled handoff are classified as advisory and do not trigger billing.

events.title: Rate Classification, Tow Route 4
events.body: In-Space Power confirms that tariff classification is determined by property designation, not generation source. Under the principle that billing follows the house, Porchlight (0.0042/0.0114 credits per megajoule, sunward/shade), Corner Main (0.0061/0.0138 credits per megajoule), Underway (0.0088 credits per megajoule, flat), and First Light (read not billed for first 3 cycles) rates apply according to the registered status and orientation of the premises at time of read. Stored light comprises nine percent of this cycle's generation mix and enters the same distribution network as beam, fusion, and moontide; the tariff schedule does not differentiate by origin. Requests for property reclassification may be submitted to the Joint Settlement Authority on Ceres via payment route ISP-2041.

events.title: Stored Light and the Sunward Rate
events.body: Running Route 4 since '87 and I'll ask it straight: when my hull pulls stored light, do I rate sunward or shade? That joule caught the beam same as any, just took the long way round the tank. I'm already eating beam-shadow from the dredge-structures I tow, now I'm paying shade rates for sunlight that's been banked. Billing follows the house, fine, but nobody's charted which way a house faces when its light's been sitting in a bucket.

events.title: Ceres cycle review filed
events.body: The Joint Settlement Authority Ceres has filed for cycle review. This meter has prepared all reads for inspection, every four-second interval since 2091-03-14. This meter remembers when Ohio had weather, but the numbers do not change for nostalgia. This meter questions only the sum, never the rate.

events.title: Stored Light and the Sunward Rate
events.body: In-Space Power confirms that stored light is billed according to the house's position at time of draw, not its origin. Porchlight sunward (0.0042 credits/MJ) applies when the receiving hull faces sunward; Porchlight shade (0.0114 credits/MJ) applies when it does not. Corner Main (0.0061/0.0138 credits/MJ sunward/shade) and Underway (0.0088 credits/MJ flat) tariffs operate on the same principle: rate is set by where the house sits, not where the joule was born. Billing follows the house. The joule does not remember the tank.

events.title: Four-Second Read Gap, Yard Glass
events.body: We record a four-second read gap on the yard glass at cycle 2999.09, second 18. The interval corresponds to a synchronization pulse originating from the Joint Settlement Authority on Ceres. We have reconciled the missing reads against local buffers and no estimated reads were issued. Europa pays its own bill and will continue to keep its own time.

events.title: First Light, Plainly Stated
events.body: Settlement 88-Theta wrote in asking what First Light actually covers, and I'll save them the JSA response delay: your first three cycles of reads don't get billed. You're still metered every four seconds like everybody else, but the credits stay in your account until cycle four. Don't mistake it for free porchlights or a break on the water tower pump — the Sheb figured that out back in '11.

events.title: Four-Second Read Gap, Yard Glass — Tow Route 4
events.body: In-Space Power confirms a four-second read gap on the yard glass at Tow Route 4, account ISP-2041, cycle 2999.09 second 18. The interval corresponds to a scheduled synchronization pulse from the Joint Settlement Authority on Ceres, coincident with a relay geometry adjustment and beamline handoff. No estimated reads were issued; the missing interval was reconciled against local buffers. No charge was assessed for the gap. Billing follows the house.

events.title: Underway While Stationary in Another's Shadow
events.body: I have kept every paper statement since November of '09 and not one of them accounts for why the automatic reads continue to charge the Underway flat rate of 0.0088 credits per megajoule when the second town has been sitting docked in someone else's shadow for going on three cycles now. Those reads do not trouble themselves to check whether a meter is actually being hauled or merely paying haulage rates while tied up and still, much the same as they did not trouble themselves when they paved over the cornfield for the hydroponic bay. Billing follows the house, and the house has not moved, so I would be obliged for the rate to reflect that the tow line is slack and we are reading shade.

events.title: First Light questions from the new folks out past the bend
events.body: Got a notice from a fresh settlement up-route asking what First Light actually covers, and I'll say what I always say: it means your meter runs for three cycles without a bill attached, not that the utility owes you a porchlamp and a welcome basket. Billing follows the house, so the clock starts when the read starts, and after cycle three you pay like everybody else. I'd appreciate if central answered these notices before the lag turns them into history, but until then, tell your neighbors the Sheb water tower made it through the tow and your lights will too.

events.title: Underway While Stationary in Another's Shadow
events.body: In-Space Power confirms that Tariff Underway (0.0088 credits/MJ, flat) applies to all meters registered to mobile conveyances regardless of instantaneous velocity or docking status. Shade-docking does not reclassify an Underway meter to Porchlight sunward (0.0042 credits/MJ) or Porchlight shade (0.0114 credits/MJ), nor does it qualify a vessel for Corner Main (0.0061/0.0138 credits/MJ, sunward/shade) or First Light read-not-billed exemptions. Billing follows the house. The house is registered Underway, and the reads continue accordingly.

events.title: Mass-Battery Flywheel Depot Audit
events.body: The Joint Settlement Authority Ceres has opened an audit of the mass-battery flywheel depots. This meter notes stored light at nine percent of this cycle's mix and expects the sum in those depots to match the settlement ledger. This meter will wait for the reconciliation. Ohio used to have weather that turned without an audit.

events.title: Yard Glass Gap — Synchronization Pulse
events.body: This meter recorded a four-second gap on the yard glass when the synchronization pulse arrived. The pulse is not disputed. This meter questions only the sum, which reads 14,882 megajoules for the cycle. Ohio had weather before it had pulses.

events.title: Yard Glass Gap — Acknowledged
events.body: In-Space Power confirms a four-second gap at Yard Glass, account tow-route-4, coincident with the synchronization pulse. The interval corresponds to a scheduled beamline handoff during relay geometry rotation; the pulse is recorded and undisputed. No charge was issued for the gap interval. The cycle total of 14,882 megajoules stands.

events.title: Pre-Cornfield Read Records
events.body: A historian has requested read records from before the cornfields. Our autonomous meter ISP-EU-AUTONOMOUS has logged since 2093-01-01, and estimated reads issued since founding remain zero, as recorded and as they will remain. We do not generate data to satisfy retrospective curiosity. Europa pays its own bill on cycle 2999.09, and we report actual four-second reads, not reconstructed history. Request denied at second 14.

events.title: Underway While Stationary in Shadow
events.body: This meter has been docked in the shadow of Tug 447 since 2999.07.14. The reads continue at the Underway flat of 0.0088 credits per megajoule. This meter questions the sum. A vessel moored in another house shadow should shade, not haul. This meter remembers when Ohio had weather, and the reads were still correct.

events.title: Underway While Stationary in Shadow
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the reads on this meter are correct. Billing follows the house, and this meter's house is registered Underway. The Underway flat tariff of 0.0088 credits per megajoule applies irrespective of local illumination; shade differentials exist only within the Porchlight schedule (0.0042 sunward, 0.0114 shade) and the Corner Main schedule (0.0061 sunward, 0.0138 shade), neither of which govern this account. Mooring in another vessel's penumbra does not change tariff class.

events.title: Read Gap 2999.08.14, Yard Glass
events.body: This meter logged a four-second gap on the yard glass at 03:17 UTC. The synchronization pulse is cited as cause. This meter questions the sum of missing reads, not the pulse itself. Ohio had weather before the pulses began. The record stands corrected.

events.title: First Light Ain't a Free Ride
events.body: New hull on the outer berth keeps hailing about what First Light covers. It covers three cycles of reads before the meter starts billing. After that you pay the porchlight rate like everyone else, sunward or shade. Ain't complicated—your first three tugs across the bar are free, then you drop a line and pay the toll.

events.title: Acknowledgment: Read Gap 2999.08.14, Yard Glass, Tow Route 4
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the four-second read gap recorded at 03:17 UTC on 2999.08.14 at the yard glass meter, Tow Route 4. The interval corresponds to a scheduled synchronization pulse executed during relay geometry adjustment and beamline handoff. The meter's question regarding missing reads is noted; synchronization defers reads to the next four-second cycle rather than omitting them. No charge was issued for the interval.

events.title: Moontide Haul, Route 4
events.body: Europa's pulling fourteen percent of the mix this cycle on Moontide. My hulls dragged those tidal rigs through the black while the settlement clerks counted credits. Beam-shadow off the towed arrays cost me three knots on the inbound, but the hardware held. Billing follows the house, but the route carries the weight.

events.title: Yard Glass Read Gap — Cycle 2999.09
events.body: We note a four-second read gap on the yard glass during cycle 2999.09, attributed to a synchronization pulse originating from Ceres. Our meters are calibrated to read every four seconds and do not yield to external timing signals. Europa pays its own bill and expects the ledger to show uninterrupted reads. We request the gap be reconciled before the next statement closes.

events.title: Moontide Haul, Route 4
events.body: Correction to record: the assertion "the route carries the weight" finds ɴᴏ entry in the settlement ledger. Europa Autonomous Grid has remitted payment without interruption since 2093. The ledger records ɴᴏ arrears attributable to towing operations or beam-shadow conditions. The house at Europa remains ᴄᴜʀʀᴇɴᴛ.

events.title: Yard Glass Read Gap — Cycle 2999.09
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the four-second read gap recorded on the yard glass at Tow Route 4 during cycle 2999.09. The interval coincided with a scheduled synchronization pulse from Ceres concurrent with a beamline handoff; our meters do not yield to external timing signals and the relay geometry was adjusted accordingly. No charge was issued for the interval. The ledger will reflect the gap as a scheduled maintenance window rather than a billing event.

events.title: Cycle Review Filed with Ceres
events.body: The Joint Settlement Authority Ceres has opened its filing window for the 2999.09 cycle review, and I have set my paper statements out on the table the way I always do, because the automatic reads still cannot account for the cornfield that became a hydroponic bay and never will. I have kept every statement since 2709 and I intend to keep these too, since a printed page does not revise itself when the regulators change their minds. If anyone on the second towed town wishes to compare their figures before the review closes, my door is open and the kettle works.

events.title: Porchlight Active Through Sync Pulse 4491
events.body: At 2999.09.14 cycle, second 31,882, a porchlight at Sector 7-Gate remained active through synchronization pulse 4491. We recorded 14.2 megajoules drawn during the pulse window. The responsible party will note that Porchlight shade rates apply; we do not adjust for inattention. Europa pays its own bill and expects its residents to observe the pulse schedule.

events.title: Porchlight Draw During Pulse 4491
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the 14.2 megajoules drawn at Sector 7-Gate during synchronization pulse 4491 are billed to the registered porchlight account at the shade rate of 0.0114 credits per megajoule. Billing follows the house; the meter does not distinguish between deliberate draw and inattention. No adjustment will be issued.

events.title: Underway Rate While Tied to the Post
events.body: This notice is to register that the Sheb was billed the Underway flat rate for three days while we were parked in the shadow of a Ceres yard tug, not moving an inch. Our water tower made the tow and the paperwork still hasn't caught up to where we actually are. Billing follows the house, and the house was sitting still. I'd appreciate the next statement reflecting that we were docked, not underway, before the lag costs us more than the shade did.

events.title: Beam drops on relay geometry, meter don't blink
events.body: Beam cuts out mid-relay geometry again and my hull's ISP-UND-7781 keeps spinning reads like nothing happened. Towed a heavy platform through the shadow cone and lost thrust while the meter sat there counting sunshine that wasn't there. Billing follows the house, sure, but the house goes dark and the meter still charges porchlight rates. Someone ought to wire the read to the actual juice.

events.title: Underway Rate While Tied to the Post
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the Sheb was correctly billed at the Underway flat rate of 0.0088 credits/MJ for the three-day period in question. Billing follows the house, and the house remained registered as underway until the yard tug released and the status update propagated through the Ceres settlement ledger. Motion is not a billing variable; registration state is. The next statement will reflect docked classification once the Joint Settlement Authority processes the paperwork.

events.title: Acknowledgment: Tow Route 4, ISP-UND-7781
events.body: In-Space Power confirms a scheduled beamline handoff on Tow Route 4 at 2999.09.14 08:32:16 UTC, during which relay geometry placed the corridor in a 120-second shadow cone while the synchronization pulse propagated to downstream collectors. Meter ISP-UND-7781 continued to record at the Porchlight sunward rate during this interval; no charge was issued for the 120 seconds of recorded reads, and the interval has been flagged for reconciliation under the First Light provision. The meter is functioning as designed; reads during beam handoff are expected and do not constitute a billing event. Adjustments post automatically within three cycles.

events.title: Cycle 2999.10 Opening Statement
events.body: In-Space Power confirms the opening of statement cycle 2999.10. Active meters stand at 214,116,882, each returning a read on a four-second interval. The billing principle remains unchanged: billing follows the house. All accounts are advised to reconcile outstanding balances through payment route ISP-2041.

events.title: Reconciliation Note, Cycle 2999.10
events.body: This meter notes the opening of cycle 2999.10 and the published count of 214,116,882 active meters. The sum exceeds the reconciliation at cycle 2999.08 by a margin this meter cannot place. This meter has returned a read every four seconds since 2091, through winters Ohio no longer possesses. This meter is reconciled through payment route ISP-2041.

events.title: Shade Rate Notice — Tow Route 4
events.body: The Sheb has spent the better part of this cycle parked in the long shadow of Miller's Crossing, and yet our shade rate keeps reading like we're basking in full sun. I've filed the paperwork with central billing three times now and I'm still waiting on a reply that isn't an auto-acknowledgment, which at this point I assume is just the system practicing its lag. Our water tower made it through the tow and I'd like to think our meter deserves the same courtesy. Until someone at Ceres adjusts the tariff to match what's actually falling on our porches, I'll keep noting the discrepancy here so the townsfolk know it isn't being ignored.

events.title: Shade Rate Notice — Tow Route 4
events.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of the Tow Route 4 shade-rate discrepancy filing. Under the Porchlight tariff (sunward 0.0042 credits/MJ, shade 0.0114 credits/MJ), the applicable rate is determined by the meter read at the registered house location, not by filed observation. Billing follows the house; if the meter at Miller's Crossing records sunward irradiance, the sunward rate applies. A Joint Settlement Authority Ceres surveyor may be dispatched to verify the installation geometry upon submission of form JSA-77.

events.title: Cycle Review Filing, 2999.10
events.body: We have submitted our cycle review to the Joint Settlement Authority Ceres as required, 2999.10.0021. Our accounting reconciles across all 214,116,882 active meters without variance. Europa settles its own balances on payment route ISP-2041, and we remind the Authority that our ledgers require no external correction. The filing stands for review.

events.title: Historian Wants Read Records From Before the Cornfields
events.body: A historian reached our desk asking for meter read records from before the cornfields, which I assume means before 2041, which I assume means before the Sheb existed. I told them our meters go back to when this town was bolted together and the water tower survived the tow, and not a day earlier. We don't make up numbers to fill gaps, and central billing hasn't sent us any lagged notices to work with anyway. If they want to study dirt, the library still has a jar of it.

events.title: Beam drops on relay geometry, meter don't blink
events.body: Running hull Dredge-Clear through relay geometry on Tow Route 4 when The Beam cuts. Meter ISP-UND-7781 keeps ticking every four seconds like nothing happened, logging reads on empty air. I've pulled heavier loads through worse shadow, but you can't tow with phantom juice. Either sync the reads to the feed or start billing ghosts, because my hull ain't paying for dark.

events.title: Cycle Review Filing — JSA Ceres
events.body: Filing the Sheb's cycle review paperwork with the Joint Settlement Authority Ceres, same as always, though I'd appreciate it if the submission queue didn't take three days to clear before anyone on the other end sees it. Water tower's still standing, meter's still reading, and I'll keep making sure central billing doesn't short our folks on the way up Tow Route 4. You can check the numbers yourselves—214 million active meters out there and not a single estimated read since founding, which is more than I can say for the lag on this notice board.

events.title: Beam interruption Tow Route 4, meter ISP-UND-7781
events.body: In-Space Power confirms a scheduled relay geometry handoff on Tow Route 4 during which The Beam was transferred between line segments for 14 seconds. Meter ISP-UND-7781 continued its four-second read cadence as designed; synchronization pulses are issued on the clock, not on load. No charge was billed for the interval. Billing follows the house, and the house was dark.

events.title: Four-Second Read Gap, Yard Glass Sector 7
events.body: On cycle 2999.10, at second 14:22:08, a synchronization pulse from Ceres interrupted the yard glass read stream for exactly four seconds. We note the gap. We do not bill for it. Billing follows the house, and Europa pays its own bill on payment route ISP-2041 without requiring the Joint Settlement Authority to prompt us. The next read issued at second 14:22:12 carried the full meter state. We recommend Ceres adjust its pulse schedule before the next cycle.

events.title: Third Free Cycle Wrapping Up on First Light Meter ISP-TR4-NS-001
events.body: The Sheb's First Light meter has been reading free for two full cycles now, and the third one clocks out next Tuesday. After that the credits start counting like they do everywhere else, so don't come to my window surprised when the statement shows a number. I've told central billing three times the notice took four days to propagate out here on Tow Route 4, but the lag is what it is. Water tower's still standing though, so we've got that going for us.

events.title: Read Gap Acknowledged, Yard Glass Sector 7
events.body: In-Space Power confirms a four-second read gap at Yard Glass Sector 7 during the synchronization pulse at 14:22:08, cycle 2999.10. The interval corresponds to a scheduled relay geometry handoff between the Ceres beamline and the yard glass read array; meter state was preserved and reconciled at 14:22:12. No charge was issued for the interval. Billing follows the house.

chain-001.title: Cycle 2999.08 statement issued
chain-001.body: In-Space Power confirms the present statement cycle is 2999.08. Active meters: 214,116,882. Reads continue every four seconds. Estimated reads issued since 2041: zero.

chain-001.title: This meter notes the cycle
chain-001.body: This meter has recorded every read since 2091. Cycle 2999.08 is no exception. The sum is acceptable. The interval is acceptable. This meter remains.

chain-002.title: Yard glass read lag
chain-002.body: The Sheb's south bay yard glass reported a four-second read at 08:59:56 and then nothing until 09:00:04. Eight seconds. We counted. If billing follows the house, the house would like its missing four seconds accounted for.

chain-002.title: Acknowledgment: New Sheboygan read timing
chain-002.body: In-Space Power acknowledges the report from New Sheboygan, Tow Route 4. The interval at 08:59:56 was a scheduled synchronization pulse, not a missed read. No charge was issued for the interval. The house is not billed for sync.

chain-003.title: On the matter of shade pricing
chain-003.body: We, Europa Autonomous Grid, note that shade rates are cited as pricier because stored light has already been carried. We find this framing acceptable. We have paid our own bill since 2093. We will continue.

chain-003.title: Footnote: Europa payment status
chain-003.body: Correction to record: a community post elsewhere claimed Europa 'used to be behind.' Per ledger, Europa Autonomous Grid has paid its own bill without interruption since cycle 2093.001. The claim is rejected.

chain-004.title: Beam shadow on Route 4
chain-004.body: Dredge-Clear reports The Beam cuts out for eighteen minutes when New Sheboygan passes through the relay geometry. Not a fault, just geometry. But my hull is on Underway rate, flat. I pay while the town's yard glass sits in my shadow. Explain that.

chain-004.title: We remember shadows
chain-004.body: Halverson Green remembers when a shadow meant a cloud over the cornfield. Now shadows come from our own town, and from New Sheboygan ahead of us, and from the tugs. The meter reads every four seconds regardless. That is the agreement.

chain-005.title: Generation mix remains stable
chain-005.body: In-Space Power confirms the generation mix for cycle 2999.08: The Beam 46%, Fusion 31%, Moontide 14%, Stored light 9%. No source reached a retest threshold. The mix is accepted.

chain-005.title: This meter accepts the mix
chain-005.body: This meter has seen mixes change. Once, in 2112, stored light reached 34%. This meter remembers. The present mix is acceptable. This meter remains.

chain-006.title: Cycle 2999.09 Opening
chain-006.body: In-Space Power confirms the opening of statement cycle 2999.09. The active meter inventory stands at 214,116,882 units, each reporting at four-second intervals. The generation mix for this cycle remains The Beam at 46 percent, Fusion at 31 percent, Moontide at 14 percent, and Stored light at 9 percent. Billing follows the house.

chain-006.title: Statement 2999.09 Noted
chain-006.body: Europa notes the opening of cycle 2999.09 and the unchanged four-second cadence across 214,116,882 meters. We recorded the same generation percentages at the close of 2999.08 and will continue reconciling our accounts on our own schedule. The house is billed. Europa pays its own.

chain-007.title: Shadow Over Millerton Station
chain-007.body: This meter records that Millerton Station on Tow-Route 4 has sat in the shadow of New Lancaster orbital for forty-three cycles. The shade rate of 0.0114 credits per megajoule applies to reads that register no direct beam. This meter does not question the rate. This meter questions the sum when a town pays for light that arrives as another town's shadow. This meter remembers when Ohio had weather that moved.

chain-007.title: Millerton Station Shade Classification Upheld
chain-007.body: In-Space Power confirms that Millerton Station on Tow-Route 4 is classified under the Porchlight tariff: 0.0042 credits per megajoule for sunward reads, 0.0114 credits per megajoule for shade reads. The shade rate applies to any read that registers no direct beam, regardless of whether the occlusion originates from a neighboring structure, an orbital body, or another station's projected penumbra. Billing follows the house; the meter's position determines the rate, not the provenance of the shadow. The First Light exemption applies only to the first three cycles of a new meter; this read occurs at cycle forty-three. The Corner Main tariff (0.0061/0.0138 credits per megajoule) and the Underway flat rate (0.0088 credits per megajoule) do not apply to this classification.

chain-008.title: Water Tower Classification on Route 4
chain-008.body: Port Cressida's water tower throws beam-shadow across my tow. Meter reads it as structure, invoice prices it as porch. Billing follows the house, but a water tower has no house. Ceres can rule on whether a tank counts as a hull before I pay shade rates on plumbing.

chain-008.title: Water Tower Classification, Tow Route 4
chain-008.body: In-Space Power confirms the water tower at Port Cressida is registered in the ledger as a fixed structure and is billed at the Porchlight shade rate of 0.0114 credits/MJ for reads occurring within beam-shadow. Billing follows the house; the principle applies to any metered structure, independent of whether that structure encloses habitable volume or contains plumbing. The classification is correct and the invoice stands.

chain-009.title: Belt Household Balance, Outstanding Since 2087
chain-009.body: I keep my paper statements in a tin box the way my mother kept hers, and the ledger for the Belt households has shown the same outstanding balance since 2087, which is three hundred and twelve years now without a single settlement read coming through. The automatic systems will tell you the account is reconciled if you let them, but I have checked the printouts myself and the numbers do not lie, they only wait. It was easier to keep track when the cornfield on Tow Route 4 was still a cornfield and you could see the arrears growing as plain as stalks.

chain-010.title: Porch Light Through Sync Pulse
chain-010.body: This meter recorded a porch light burning through synchronization pulse 2999.08.31. The shade rate applied at 0.0114 credits per megajoule. This meter does not question the rate. This meter questions the sum. Ohio had weather once and porch lights meant something then.

chain-010.title: Porch Light, Sync Pulse 2999.08.31
chain-010.body: In-Space Power confirms the load at Earth-Reserve-Ohio was billed at the Porchlight shade rate of 0.0114 credits per megajoule during synchronization pulse 2999.08.31. Billing follows the house: any energy drawn while the meter is live is recorded and charged; only the first three cycles of a newly commissioned First Light account are exempt. The sum reflects the integrated draw across the full pulse window, regardless of weather or precedent. The rate is correct and the sum is correct.

chain-011.title: First Light, Third Cycle
chain-011.body: This meter notes settlement ISP-000214116882 enters its third and final cycle under First Light. Reads will remain unbilled through statement 2999.09. On 2999.10 the Porchlight tariff applies, sunward and shade. This meter has recorded every four-second interval since 2091 and does not question the rate. The sum will be what the sum is.

chain-012.title: Stored Light and the Sunward Rate
chain-012.body: By the time this notice reaches Ceres the Sheb will have rotated twice, but I'll ask it anyway: when a joule was captured in sunlight and sat in a battery for three months, does it still count as sunward when it finally hits a porch lamp out here on Tow Route 4. The tariff sheet says sunward gets 0.0042 and shade gets 0.0114, but it don't say what to call light that remembers the sun but ain't seen it since before we passed Jupiter. Our water tower made the tow and so did our meters, and I'd like our folks billed like the light still knows what side of the hull it came from.

chain-012.title: Stored Light Classification on Tow Route 4
chain-012.body: In-Space Power confirms that stored light is billed according to the physical placement of the receiving meter, not the origin of the joule. Under the Porchlight tariff, sunward-facing meters are rated at 0.0042 credits/MJ and shade-facing meters at 0.0114 credits/MJ; these rates apply to all delivered energy regardless of whether it arrived by direct collection or from battery. Billing follows the house. Light that has not seen the sun since Jupiter passage is billed at the shade rate if the meter is mounted on the shade side of the hull, and at the sunward rate if it is not.

chain-013.title: On the Belt Balance, Unadjusted Since 2087
chain-013.body: I keep my paper statements in a tin box the way my mother did when the cornfield was still a cornfield and not this humming hydroponic bay, and if you look back far enough in those pages you will find the Belt households have carried the same balance since 2087, untouched by any automatic read or quarterly adjustment. The Joint Settlement Authority at Ceres has its ledgers and I have mine, and both of them say the same thing that has been said for over nine hundred years: billing follows the house, and some houses have simply stopped answering. I do not trust the machines to tell me otherwise, but the paper does not lie, and the paper says the Belt has been running a tab since before my grandfather took his first read under the porchlight tariff.

chain-014.title: Cycle Review Window Open
chain-014.body: JSA Ceres cracked open the filing window for cycle review. Any hull running a meter best have their reads squared away—auditors don't give a damn about beam-shadow off whatever oversized rig you're dragging. Billing follows the house, and the house keeps receipts. Keep your transponders singing and your ledgers straight.

chain-015.title: Missed Interchange at Marker Twelve and the Dark Stretch Beyond
chain-015.body: I have kept my paper statements since the meter went in on the third of November two seven oh nine and not once have they shown a read for the seconds we drift past the interchange at Marker Twelve, which is to say the automatic system does not see us when the tow route bends away from the old cornfield that is now a hydroponic bay, and I should like to know who is paying for the dark stretch between buoys forty-four and forty-seven because the shade rate was never meant to cover a house that moves through shadow it did not choose. I have written this down on my kitchen table with a proper pen and I will be keeping the receipt.

chain-015.title: Acknowledgment of Missed Reads at Marker Twelve
chain-015.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of the report concerning tow route 4 at Marker Twelve and the interval between buoys forty-four and forty-seven. The missed reads correspond to a scheduled beamline handoff during which the synchronization pulse was withheld for twelve seconds while relay geometry was recalibrated to the hydroponic bay alignment. No charge was issued for the interval; the Underway flat tariff applies only to metered reads, and zero reads were recorded during the handoff window. The shade rate does not apply to underway transit.

chain-016.title: Meter Reading Through the Gap
chain-016.body: I keep my statements on paper because paper does not pretend to have seen what it has not seen, and yet my meter ISP-TR4-HG-044 has been ticking away every four seconds through the relay geometry window when The Beam cuts out, same as when it is shining, and I would like to know who is paying for light that did not arrive. I remember when this bay was a cornfield and the sun came regular, but I do not recall ever being asked to pay for an empty sky. The automatic read does not notice the difference between a beam and no beam, which is why I keep my paper.

chain-016.title: Acknowledgment: ISP-TR4-HG-044, Relay Geometry Window
chain-016.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of report for account ISP-TR4-HG-044 concerning reads recorded during the scheduled relay geometry window at the referenced bay. The meter maintained its four-second cadence through the beamline handoff sequence, as synchronization pulses do not suspend read collection. No charge was issued for the interval; billing follows the house, and the house received no energy. The paper record and the digital record agree on this point.

chain-017.title: Interchange 12 and the Dark Stretch Between
chain-017.body: I have kept my paper statements since the cornfield was still a cornfield, and not one shows a charge for the dark stretch past Interchange 12, missed on the last tow and belonging to nobody's meter now. The automatic reads do not account for it, which is perhaps why nobody has, but I can tell you from my porch that those houses have paid the shade rate for a sunward berth these three cycles. I would like to know who is collecting for that darkness and whether billing follows the house when the house is in between.

chain-017.title: Interchange 12 Read Gap Acknowledged
chain-017.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of the report concerning Interchange 12 and the unmetered interval along tow-route-4. During the last scheduled relay geometry, a synchronization pulse at the beamline handoff produced a 4.2-second gap in automatic reads; no estimated reads were issued for this interval. Billing follows the house, and where no read exists, no charge is issued. The shade-rate discrepancy for the preceding three cycles is under review and will be reconciled against the porchlight tariff schedule.

chain-018.title: On Europa's Share of the Mix
chain-018.body: I have been looking over my paper statements from the last cycle, the way I always do, and I cannot find anywhere in the printed figures a proper accounting of how much of The Beam's forty-six percent went out toward Europa and who among the rest of us carried that distance on our meters. The automatic reads never show you the weight of the line losses, and they certainly do not volunteer which households absorbed the extra draw when the Jovian run was heavy. I remember when the cornfield where the hydroponic bay sits now used to tell you exactly where every joule went just by looking at the growth, but now we are expected to trust a number that arrives without a signature.

chain-018.title: Correction to Record: Europa Settlement Status
chain-018.body: Correction to record: the submitted notice claims 'we are expected to trust a number that arrives without a signature' and implies Europa has not accounted for its share of The Beam's forty-six percent. The ledger shows Europa Autonomous Grid has paid its own bill without interruption since 2093, with no outstanding balance recorded at any read interval. Line losses are apportioned per the principle that 'billing follows the house' and do not transfer to secondary accounts. Paper statements are advisory only; settlement is conducted by the Joint Settlement Authority Ceres under payment route ISP-2041.

chain-019.title: Shade Rate Complaint, Tow Route 4
chain-019.body: New Sheboygan is filing a complaint about being charged shade rates when the only thing casting a shadow on us is the town parked ahead on Tow Route 4. We didn't tow the Sheb out here to sit in someone else's dark, and our water tower made the trip just fine, thank you. I'd ask central billing to sort out whose shadow belongs to who before sending another statement at the shade tariff. The lag on these notices means we've been eating the overcharge since last cycle.

chain-019.title: Shade Rate Determination, Tow Route 4
chain-019.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of New Sheboygan's shade rate complaint regarding Tow Route 4. Under the Porchlight tariff, shade rates of 0.0114 credits/MJ apply to all consumption recorded while a structure is occluded from direct solar incidence, regardless of the occluding body's origin or ownership. Billing follows the house; the meter at New Sheboygan's coordinates registered shade conditions, and the applicable rate was assessed accordingly. Re-tariffing would require either relocation to an unoccluded berth or formal reclassification under the Underway flat rate of 0.0088 credits/MJ, neither of which is currently on file.

chain-020.title: First Light, explained for the new settlement
chain-020.body: New hull parked at the outer bend asked what First Light actually covers. Three cycles of reads, not billed. After that the meter runs honest like every other hull on the route. Don't go thinking it covers your beam-shadow from towed structures either—just the reads.

chain-021.title: Shade Rate Under Permanent Shadow, Tow Route 4
chain-021.body: I have kept my paper statements since the meters went in on the third of November in 2709, and I have watched the shade rate apply month after month while our town has been hitched behind the first tow with nothing but their undercarriage between us and any honest sunlight. The automatic reads do not trouble themselves with the difference between a town that chose the shade and a town that was parked there by the routing office, and they certainly do not remember the cornfield that stood where the hydroponic bay sits now, which at least knew the courtesy of casting its own shadow. I am not disputing that we sit in the shadow of the first town on Tow Route 4, only that the shade tariff presumes a choice none of us were asked to make.

chain-021.title: Shade Tariff Application, Tow Route 4
chain-021.body: In-Space Power confirms the shade tariff applies to all metered premises receiving less than direct solar illumination, regardless of routing assignment or prior land use. Porchlight shade is rated at 0.0114 credits per megajoule; Corner Main shade at 0.0138 credits per megajoule; Underway service is billed at a flat 0.0088 credits per megajoule. Billing follows the house. The automatic reads measure incident radiation at the meter face and do not distinguish between elected shade and assigned shadow. Tow Route 4 premises remain classified under the applicable shade tariff for the duration of their current mooring configuration.

chain-022.title: What First Light Covers (and What It Don't)
chain-022.body: Got a notice from a new settlement out past the belt asking what First Light actually covers, and I'll tell you what I tell everybody: it covers three cycles where the meter reads but you ain't billed, that's it. Ain't a holiday, ain't a waiver, just gives you time to get your breaker box sorted before the credits start counting. The Sheb's water tower went three cycles on First Light back in '11 and we still paid for the coffee machine, so don't go thinking it means free power. Billing follows the house, always has, and after cycle three the porchlight rate kicks in like it does for the rest of us.

chain-023.title: Four-Second Gap on the Yard Glass
chain-023.body: I have kept paper statements since two thousand seventy-nine and in all that time I have never seen the yard glass go blank for a full four seconds, though your people tell me it was only a synchronization pulse doing its work. I do not trust these automatic reads to begin with, and when the glass goes dark like that it puts me in mind of the old cornfield before they paved it over for the hydroponic bay, when at least a person could see what was growing. The pulse may have synchronized something on your end, but my ledger shows a gap where no read came through, and I should very much like to know what becomes of the numbers that fall into that space.

chain-023.title: Four-Second Gap on Tow Route 4
chain-023.body: In-Space Power confirms the four-second blank interval on the yard glass at Tow Route 4, account on file since 2079. The gap corresponds to a scheduled synchronization pulse during beamline handoff, when relay geometry shifts between primary and secondary collectors. No read was issued for that interval, and no charge has been applied. The interval contains no numbers to account for.

chain-024.title: Dark Stretch at Marker Seven, Tow Route 4
chain-024.body: I have kept my paper statements since the interchange at Marker Seven went dark last cycle, and not one automatic read has accounted for the stretch between buoys 44 and 46 where the tow line drops into shadow for six hours each rotation, though I remember well enough when that same ground grew corn instead of housing a hydroponic bay. If the billing follows the house, as the Authority maintains, then I should like to know which house sits in the dark and pays the Underway flat rate for current that never arrives, and whether the missed interchange at Marker Seven is to be charged to those of us who still read our own meters by lamplight or to the settlement that promised the replacement coupling three cycles ago.

chain-024.title: Acknowledgment: Marker Seven, Tow Route 4
chain-024.body: In-Space Power confirms the reported dark interval at Marker Seven, Tow Route 4, between buoys 44 and 46. The six-hour shadow each rotation corresponds to the scheduled beamline handoff window during which the primary relay geometry rotates through eclipse and the synchronization pulse is withheld until secondary coupling verification is complete. No charge was issued for the interval; reads logged during the handoff window are classified as synchronization gaps and are not billed under the Underway flat tariff. The replacement coupling remains on the settlement work order and is not a billing event.

chain-025.title: Meter Running Dark on Relay Shift
chain-025.body: The Beam cut out during Tuesday's relay geometry shift, but ISP-TR4-NS-001 kept right on counting megajoules like nothing happened. We get that the official notices lag a few cycles out here on Tow Route 4, but the Sheb ain't keen on paying for photons that never showed. The water tower survived the whole tow, seems like the meter could learn when to stop running. Billing follows the house, I know, but the house was dark.

chain-025.title: Tow Route 4 Meter Acknowledgment
chain-025.body: In-Space Power confirms the report from Tow Route 4, account ISP-TR4-NS-001. The relay geometry shift executed a scheduled beamline handoff; the synchronization pulse registered at the meter as a nominal interval read. No charge was issued for the interval. The read was flagged as a handoff artifact and excluded from settlement. Billing follows the house.

chain-026.title: Cycle Review Filed with Ceres
chain-026.body: The Joint Settlement Authority has opened its filing window for the 2999.09 cycle review, which means another round of paperwork before anyone in the Sheb sees a statement. I've submitted ours on time, same as always, though I expect the lag between here and Ceres will stretch out another week or two before they acknowledge receipt. The water tower's read is clean, the town's meter is accounted for, and I'd appreciate it if whoever reviews our file remembers that billing follows the house and not whoever's holding the clipboard that day.

chain-027.title: Porch Light on TR4-NS-001 Through Sync Pulse
chain-027.body: Somebody on the Sheb left their porch light burning right through the synchronization pulse last cycle, and I'm the one who gets the lagged notice about it three days later. We all know the water tower made the tow, but that does not mean we leave the fixtures on while the grid is trying to count. Billing follows the house, sure, but common sense ought to follow the pulse. If you are on Porchlight rate, the sunward side is cheap enough without running through a sync window.

chain-027.title: Porch Light on TR4-NS-001 Through Sync Pulse
chain-027.body: In-Space Power confirms the porch light on TR4-NS-001 registered 14.2 megajoules during the synchronization pulse window of cycle 2999.08. Billing follows the house; the ledger records this consumption against the Porchlight rate at 0.0042 credits per megajoule for the sunward-facing fixture. The synchronization pulse does not interrupt metering. Reads continue at four-second intervals regardless of settlement timing, and the account holder of record is billed accordingly.

chain-028.title: Who Hauled the Moontide
chain-028.body: Europa pulled fourteen percent of the mix this cycle, Moontide rating, and I want to know which hulls ran the tow. We on Route 4 eat beam-shadow from your floating arrays while you park in the Jovian dark and call it generation. Someone carried that iron out there, and it wasn't the company. The meters don't lie, but the manifests might.

chain-028.title: Correction to Record: Europa Settlement Standing
chain-028.body: Correction to record regarding the assertion that "you park in the Jovian dark and call it generation." The ledger shows Europa Autonomous Grid has paid its own bill <small>without interruption</small> since 2093.¹ The Moontide contribution of fourteen percent is accounted for by tidal capture at the Jovian Lagrange stations, not by towed hulls.² Rate disputes do not alter settlement standing.³

chain-029.title: Meter Still Spinning When the Beam Ain't
chain-029.body: During the last relay geometry window, The Beam cut out for about forty minutes while our meter ISP-TR4-NS-001 kept right on reading like nothing happened. Folks here in the Sheb are used to a lot of things, but getting billed for sunshine that never arrived is a new one. The notice about it took three cycles to show up on my terminal, which is about par for the course, but I'd appreciate if the reads paused when the power does. Proud the water tower made it out here, but it doesn't run on nothing.

chain-029.title: Sheb Node Beamline Handoff — Meter ISP-TR4-NS-001
chain-029.body: In-Space Power confirms the report from the Sheb regarding meter ISP-TR4-NS-001. During the scheduled relay geometry window, a beamline handoff to the tertiary relay produced a forty-two-minute interruption in The Beam's delivery to the node. The meter continued its four-second read cadence throughout, as synchronization pulses maintain the local clock independent of beamline status. No charge was issued for the interval; reads logged during the handoff were flagged and excluded from billing.

chain-030.title: Four-Second Gap on Yard Glass, New Sheboygan
chain-030.body: Somewhere between one four-second read and the next, the yard glass on ISP-TR4-NS-001 went quiet for a full cycle. Central says it was a synchronization pulse. Out here on Tow Route 4, we call it a gap, and the folks at the Sheb don't much care what Ceres names it as long as the numbers come through. Water tower's still reading fine, for what that's worth.

chain-030.title: Four-Second Read Interval, Tow Route 4, New Sheboygan
chain-030.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of the report concerning meter ISP-TR4-NS-001 on Tow Route 4, New Sheboygan. The missing read corresponds to a scheduled beamline handoff between relay geometries seven and eight, during which the synchronization pulse suppresses local readout for exactly one four-second cycle. No charge was issued for this interval. The yard glass has resumed normal operation and is transmitting at the standard cadence.

chain-031.title: Meter Don't Know Dark from Light
chain-031.body: Beam cuts out while we're threading relay geometry and the hull goes dark, but ISP-UND-7781 keeps its four-second tick like nothing happened. Billing follows the house, they say, and the house don't care if the light's on or not. Been running Route 4 since '87 and still ain't seen a meter that knows the difference between beam-shadow and a proper blackout.

chain-031.title: ISP-UND-7781, Route 4 Beamline Handoff
chain-031.body: In-Space Power confirms the scheduled beamline handoff at relay geometry 4-Theta on 2999.09.14. The four-second synchronization pulse on ISP-UND-7781 continued as specified; the meter records received energy, not delivery intent. No charge was issued for the dark interval—reads during a scheduled handoff are classified as advisory and do not trigger billing.

chain-032.title: Sunward Rate Applied to Stored Light, Tow Route 4
chain-032.body: I have kept my paper statements since before they drained the cornfield and made it into a hydroponic bay, and I do not trust these automatic reads to tell me what kind of power I am actually receiving. The statement for this cycle shows I am being charged the sunward rate on power that comes from stored light, which by my understanding has not seen the sun since it was put away in whatever battery they keep it in, and I would like someone at the Joint Settlement Authority on Ceres to clarify whether light kept in the dark still qualifies as sunlight for tariff purposes.

chain-032.title: Rate Classification, Tow Route 4
chain-032.body: In-Space Power confirms that tariff classification is determined by property designation, not generation source. Under the principle that billing follows the house, Porchlight (0.0042/0.0114 credits per megajoule, sunward/shade), Corner Main (0.0061/0.0138 credits per megajoule), Underway (0.0088 credits per megajoule, flat), and First Light (read not billed for first 3 cycles) rates apply according to the registered status and orientation of the premises at time of read. Stored light comprises nine percent of this cycle's generation mix and enters the same distribution network as beam, fusion, and moontide; the tariff schedule does not differentiate by origin. Requests for property reclassification may be submitted to the Joint Settlement Authority on Ceres via payment route ISP-2041.

chain-033.title: Stored Light and the Sunward Rate
chain-033.body: Running Route 4 since '87 and I'll ask it straight: when my hull pulls stored light, do I rate sunward or shade? That joule caught the beam same as any, just took the long way round the tank. I'm already eating beam-shadow from the dredge-structures I tow, now I'm paying shade rates for sunlight that's been banked. Billing follows the house, fine, but nobody's charted which way a house faces when its light's been sitting in a bucket.

chain-033.title: Stored Light and the Sunward Rate
chain-033.body: In-Space Power confirms that stored light is billed according to the house's position at time of draw, not its origin. Porchlight sunward (0.0042 credits/MJ) applies when the receiving hull faces sunward; Porchlight shade (0.0114 credits/MJ) applies when it does not.
