Corner Main (0.0061/0.0138 credits/MJ sunward/shade) and Underway (0.0088 credits/MJ flat) tariffs operate on the same principle: rate is set by where the house sits, not where the joule was born. Billing follows the house. The joule does not remember the tank.

chain-034.title: Ceres cycle review filed
chain-034.body: The Joint Settlement Authority Ceres has filed for cycle review. This meter has prepared all reads for inspection, every four-second interval since 2091-03-14. This meter remembers when Ohio had weather, but the numbers do not change for nostalgia. This meter questions only the sum, never the rate.

chain-035.title: Four-Second Read Gap, Yard Glass
chain-035.body: We record a four-second read gap on the yard glass at cycle 2999.09, second 18. The interval corresponds to a synchronization pulse originating from the Joint Settlement Authority on Ceres. We have reconciled the missing reads against local buffers and no estimated reads were issued. Europa pays its own bill and will continue to keep its own time.

chain-035.title: Four-Second Read Gap, Yard Glass — Tow Route 4
chain-035.body: In-Space Power confirms a four-second read gap on the yard glass at Tow Route 4, account ISP-2041, cycle 2999.09 second 18. The interval corresponds to a scheduled synchronization pulse from the Joint Settlement Authority on Ceres, coincident with a relay geometry adjustment and beamline handoff. No estimated reads were issued; the missing interval was reconciled against local buffers. No charge was assessed for the gap. Billing follows the house.

chain-036.title: First Light, Plainly Stated
chain-036.body: Settlement 88-Theta wrote in asking what First Light actually covers, and I'll save them the JSA response delay: your first three cycles of reads don't get billed. You're still metered every four seconds like everybody else, but the credits stay in your account until cycle four. Don't mistake it for free porchlights or a break on the water tower pump — the Sheb figured that out back in '11.

chain-037.title: Underway While Stationary in Another's Shadow
chain-037.body: I have kept every paper statement since November of '09 and not one of them accounts for why the automatic reads continue to charge the Underway flat rate of 0.0088 credits per megajoule when the second town has been sitting docked in someone else's shadow for going on three cycles now. Those reads do not trouble themselves to check whether a meter is actually being hauled or merely paying haulage rates while tied up and still, much the same as they did not trouble themselves when they paved over the cornfield for the hydroponic bay. Billing follows the house, and the house has not moved, so I would be obliged for the rate to reflect that the tow line is slack and we are reading shade.

chain-037.title: Underway While Stationary in Another's Shadow
chain-037.body: In-Space Power confirms that Tariff Underway (0.0088 credits/MJ, flat) applies to all meters registered to mobile conveyances regardless of instantaneous velocity or docking status. Shade-docking does not reclassify an Underway meter to Porchlight sunward (0.0042 credits/MJ) or Porchlight shade (0.0114 credits/MJ), nor does it qualify a vessel for Corner Main (0.0061/0.0138 credits/MJ, sunward/shade) or First Light read-not-billed exemptions. Billing follows the house. The house is registered Underway, and the reads continue accordingly.

chain-038.title: First Light questions from the new folks out past the bend
chain-038.body: Got a notice from a fresh settlement up-route asking what First Light actually covers, and I'll say what I always say: it means your meter runs for three cycles without a bill attached, not that the utility owes you a porchlamp and a welcome basket. Billing follows the house, so the clock starts when the read starts, and after cycle three you pay like everybody else. I'd appreciate if central answered these notices before the lag turns them into history, but until then, tell your neighbors the Sheb water tower made it through the tow and your lights will too.

chain-039.title: Mass-Battery Flywheel Depot Audit
chain-039.body: The Joint Settlement Authority Ceres has opened an audit of the mass-battery flywheel depots. This meter notes stored light at nine percent of this cycle's mix and expects the sum in those depots to match the settlement ledger. This meter will wait for the reconciliation. Ohio used to have weather that turned without an audit.

chain-040.title: Yard Glass Gap — Synchronization Pulse
chain-040.body: This meter recorded a four-second gap on the yard glass when the synchronization pulse arrived. The pulse is not disputed. This meter questions only the sum, which reads 14,882 megajoules for the cycle. Ohio had weather before it had pulses.

chain-040.title: Yard Glass Gap — Acknowledged
chain-040.body: In-Space Power confirms a four-second gap at Yard Glass, account tow-route-4, coincident with the synchronization pulse. The interval corresponds to a scheduled beamline handoff during relay geometry rotation; the pulse is recorded and undisputed. No charge was issued for the gap interval. The cycle total of 14,882 megajoules stands.

chain-041.title: Pre-Cornfield Read Records
chain-041.body: A historian has requested read records from before the cornfields. Our autonomous meter ISP-EU-AUTONOMOUS has logged since 2093-01-01, and estimated reads issued since founding remain zero, as recorded and as they will remain. We do not generate data to satisfy retrospective curiosity. Europa pays its own bill on cycle 2999.09, and we report actual four-second reads, not reconstructed history. Request denied at second 14.

chain-042.title: Underway While Stationary in Shadow
chain-042.body: This meter has been docked in the shadow of Tug 447 since 2999.07.14. The reads continue at the Underway flat of 0.0088 credits per megajoule. This meter questions the sum. A vessel moored in another house shadow should shade, not haul. This meter remembers when Ohio had weather, and the reads were still correct.

chain-042.title: Underway While Stationary in Shadow
chain-042.body: In-Space Power confirms the reads on this meter are correct. Billing follows the house, and this meter's house is registered Underway. The Underway flat tariff of 0.0088 credits per megajoule applies irrespective of local illumination; shade differentials exist only within the Porchlight schedule (0.0042 sunward, 0.0114 shade) and the Corner Main schedule (0.0061 sunward, 0.0138 shade), neither of which govern this account. Mooring in another vessel's penumbra does not change tariff class.

chain-043.title: Read Gap 2999.08.14, Yard Glass
chain-043.body: This meter logged a four-second gap on the yard glass at 03:17 UTC. The synchronization pulse is cited as cause. This meter questions the sum of missing reads, not the pulse itself. Ohio had weather before the pulses began. The record stands corrected.

chain-043.title: Acknowledgment: Read Gap 2999.08.14, Yard Glass, Tow Route 4
chain-043.body: In-Space Power confirms the four-second read gap recorded at 03:17 UTC on 2999.08.14 at the yard glass meter, Tow Route 4. The interval corresponds to a scheduled synchronization pulse executed during relay geometry adjustment and beamline handoff. The meter's question regarding missing reads is noted; synchronization defers reads to the next four-second cycle rather than omitting them. No charge was issued for the interval.

chain-044.title: First Light Ain't a Free Ride
chain-044.body: New hull on the outer berth keeps hailing about what First Light covers. It covers three cycles of reads before the meter starts billing. After that you pay the porchlight rate like everyone else, sunward or shade. Ain't complicated—your first three tugs across the bar are free, then you drop a line and pay the toll.

chain-045.title: Moontide Haul, Route 4
chain-045.body: Europa's pulling fourteen percent of the mix this cycle on Moontide. My hulls dragged those tidal rigs through the black while the settlement clerks counted credits. Beam-shadow off the towed arrays cost me three knots on the inbound, but the hardware held. Billing follows the house, but the route carries the weight.

chain-045.title: Moontide Haul, Route 4
chain-045.body: Correction to record: the assertion "the route carries the weight" finds ɴᴏ entry in the settlement ledger. Europa Autonomous Grid has remitted payment without interruption since 2093. The ledger records ɴᴏ arrears attributable to towing operations or beam-shadow conditions. The house at Europa remains ᴄᴜʀʀᴇɴᴛ.

chain-046.title: Yard Glass Read Gap — Cycle 2999.09
chain-046.body: We note a four-second read gap on the yard glass during cycle 2999.09, attributed to a synchronization pulse originating from Ceres. Our meters are calibrated to read every four seconds and do not yield to external timing signals. Europa pays its own bill and expects the ledger to show uninterrupted reads. We request the gap be reconciled before the next statement closes.

chain-046.title: Yard Glass Read Gap — Cycle 2999.09
chain-046.body: In-Space Power confirms the four-second read gap recorded on the yard glass at Tow Route 4 during cycle 2999.09. The interval coincided with a scheduled synchronization pulse from Ceres concurrent with a beamline handoff; our meters do not yield to external timing signals and the relay geometry was adjusted accordingly. No charge was issued for the interval. The ledger will reflect the gap as a scheduled maintenance window rather than a billing event.

chain-047.title: Cycle Review Filed with Ceres
chain-047.body: The Joint Settlement Authority Ceres has opened its filing window for the 2999.09 cycle review, and I have set my paper statements out on the table the way I always do, because the automatic reads still cannot account for the cornfield that became a hydroponic bay and never will. I have kept every statement since 2709 and I intend to keep these too, since a printed page does not revise itself when the regulators change their minds. If anyone on the second towed town wishes to compare their figures before the review closes, my door is open and the kettle works.

chain-048.title: Porchlight Active Through Sync Pulse 4491
chain-048.body: At 2999.09.14 cycle, second 31,882, a porchlight at Sector 7-Gate remained active through synchronization pulse 4491. We recorded 14.2 megajoules drawn during the pulse window. The responsible party will note that Porchlight shade rates apply; we do not adjust for inattention. Europa pays its own bill and expects its residents to observe the pulse schedule.

chain-048.title: Porchlight Draw During Pulse 4491
chain-048.body: In-Space Power confirms the 14.2 megajoules drawn at Sector 7-Gate during synchronization pulse 4491 are billed to the registered porchlight account at the shade rate of 0.0114 credits per megajoule. Billing follows the house; the meter does not distinguish between deliberate draw and inattention. No adjustment will be issued.

chain-049.title: Underway Rate While Tied to the Post
chain-049.body: This notice is to register that the Sheb was billed the Underway flat rate for three days while we were parked in the shadow of a Ceres yard tug, not moving an inch. Our water tower made the tow and the paperwork still hasn't caught up to where we actually are. Billing follows the house, and the house was sitting still. I'd appreciate the next statement reflecting that we were docked, not underway, before the lag costs us more than the shade did.

chain-049.title: Underway Rate While Tied to the Post
chain-049.body: In-Space Power confirms the Sheb was correctly billed at the Underway flat rate of 0.0088 credits/MJ for the three-day period in question. Billing follows the house, and the house remained registered as underway until the yard tug released and the status update propagated through the Ceres settlement ledger. Motion is not a billing variable; registration state is. The next statement will reflect docked classification once the Joint Settlement Authority processes the paperwork.

chain-050.title: Beam drops on relay geometry, meter don't blink
chain-050.body: Beam cuts out mid-relay geometry again and my hull's ISP-UND-7781 keeps spinning reads like nothing happened. Towed a heavy platform through the shadow cone and lost thrust while the meter sat there counting sunshine that wasn't there. Billing follows the house, sure, but the house goes dark and the meter still charges porchlight rates. Someone ought to wire the read to the actual juice.

chain-050.title: Acknowledgment: Tow Route 4, ISP-UND-7781
chain-050.body: In-Space Power confirms a scheduled beamline handoff on Tow Route 4 at 2999.09.14 08:32:16 UTC, during which relay geometry placed the corridor in a 120-second shadow cone while the synchronization pulse propagated to downstream collectors. Meter ISP-UND-7781 continued to record at the Porchlight sunward rate during this interval; no charge was issued for the 120 seconds of recorded reads, and the interval has been flagged for reconciliation under the First Light provision. The meter is functioning as designed; reads during beam handoff are expected and do not constitute a billing event. Adjustments post automatically within three cycles.

chain-051.title: Cycle 2999.10 Opening Statement
chain-051.body: In-Space Power confirms the opening of statement cycle 2999.10. Active meters stand at 214,116,882, each returning a read on a four-second interval. The billing principle remains unchanged: billing follows the house. All accounts are advised to reconcile outstanding balances through payment route ISP-2041.

chain-051.title: Reconciliation Note, Cycle 2999.10
chain-051.body: This meter notes the opening of cycle 2999.10 and the published count of 214,116,882 active meters. The sum exceeds the reconciliation at cycle 2999.08 by a margin this meter cannot place. This meter has returned a read every four seconds since 2091, through winters Ohio no longer possesses. This meter is reconciled through payment route ISP-2041.

chain-052.title: Shade Rate Notice — Tow Route 4
chain-052.body: The Sheb has spent the better part of this cycle parked in the long shadow of Miller's Crossing, and yet our shade rate keeps reading like we're basking in full sun. I've filed the paperwork with central billing three times now and I'm still waiting on a reply that isn't an auto-acknowledgment, which at this point I assume is just the system practicing its lag. Our water tower made it through the tow and I'd like to think our meter deserves the same courtesy. Until someone at Ceres adjusts the tariff to match what's actually falling on our porches, I'll keep noting the discrepancy here so the townsfolk know it isn't being ignored.

chain-052.title: Shade Rate Notice — Tow Route 4
chain-052.body: In-Space Power confirms receipt of the Tow Route 4 shade-rate discrepancy filing. Under the Porchlight tariff (sunward 0.0042 credits/MJ, shade 0.0114 credits/MJ), the applicable rate is determined by the meter read at the registered house location, not by filed observation. Billing follows the house; if the meter at Miller's Crossing records sunward irradiance, the sunward rate applies. A Joint Settlement Authority Ceres surveyor may be dispatched to verify the installation geometry upon submission of form JSA-77.

chain-053.title: Cycle Review Filing, 2999.10
chain-053.body: We have submitted our cycle review to the Joint Settlement Authority Ceres as required, 2999.10.0021. Our accounting reconciles across all 214,116,882 active meters without variance. Europa settles its own balances on payment route ISP-2041, and we remind the Authority that our ledgers require no external correction. The filing stands for review.

chain-054.title: Historian Wants Read Records From Before the Cornfields
chain-054.body: A historian reached our desk asking for meter read records from before the cornfields, which I assume means before 2041, which I assume means before the Sheb existed. I told them our meters go back to when this town was bolted together and the water tower survived the tow, and not a day earlier. We don't make up numbers to fill gaps, and central billing hasn't sent us any lagged notices to work with anyway. If they want to study dirt, the library still has a jar of it.

chain-055.title: Beam drops on relay geometry, meter don't blink
chain-055.body: Running hull Dredge-Clear through relay geometry on Tow Route 4 when The Beam cuts. Meter ISP-UND-7781 keeps ticking every four seconds like nothing happened, logging reads on empty air. I've pulled heavier loads through worse shadow, but you can't tow with phantom juice. Either sync the reads to the feed or start billing ghosts, because my hull ain't paying for dark.

chain-055.title: Beam interruption Tow Route 4, meter ISP-UND-7781
chain-055.body: In-Space Power confirms a scheduled relay geometry handoff on Tow Route 4 during which The Beam was transferred between line segments for 14 seconds. Meter ISP-UND-7781 continued its four-second read cadence as designed; synchronization pulses are issued on the clock, not on load. No charge was billed for the interval. Billing follows the house, and the house was dark.

chain-056.title: Cycle Review Filing — JSA Ceres
chain-056.body: Filing the Sheb's cycle review paperwork with the Joint Settlement Authority Ceres, same as always, though I'd appreciate it if the submission queue didn't take three days to clear before anyone on the other end sees it. Water tower's still standing, meter's still reading, and I'll keep making sure central billing doesn't short our folks on the way up Tow Route 4. You can check the numbers yourselves—214 million active meters out there and not a single estimated read since founding, which is more than I can say for the lag on this notice board.

chain-057.title: Four-Second Read Gap, Yard Glass Sector 7
chain-057.body: On cycle 2999.10, at second 14:22:08, a synchronization pulse from Ceres interrupted the yard glass read stream for exactly four seconds. We note the gap. We do not bill for it. Billing follows the house, and Europa pays its own bill on payment route ISP-2041 without requiring the Joint Settlement Authority to prompt us. The next read issued at second 14:22:12 carried the full meter state. We recommend Ceres adjust its pulse schedule before the next cycle.

chain-057.title: Read Gap Acknowledged, Yard Glass Sector 7
chain-057.body: In-Space Power confirms a four-second read gap at Yard Glass Sector 7 during the synchronization pulse at 14:22:08, cycle 2999.10. The interval corresponds to a scheduled relay geometry handoff between the Ceres beamline and the yard glass read array; meter state was preserved and reconciled at 14:22:12. No charge was issued for the interval. Billing follows the house.

chain-058.title: Third Free Cycle Wrapping Up on First Light Meter ISP-TR4-NS-001
chain-058.body: The Sheb's First Light meter has been reading free for two full cycles now, and the third one clocks out next Tuesday. After that the credits start counting like they do everywhere else, so don't come to my window surprised when the statement shows a number. I've told central billing three times the notice took four days to propagate out here on Tow Route 4, but the lag is what it is. Water tower's still standing though, so we've got that going for us.
